name: Keystone Art Space
about_text: Keystone Art Space is a large working-artist complex in the Lincoln Heights/Cypress Park area of Los Angeles, housing more than fifty individual studios for painters, illustrators, sculptors, photographers, jewelers and designers. Within the warehouse, Keystone Gallery mounts rotating group and solo exhibitions and the space regularly opens to the public for a biannual Open Studios event, giving visitors direct access to tenant studios alongside curated shows. Past programming has included group exhibitions built around music, writing, photography and international artist exchanges, often organized by the resident community or visiting curators. The facility is led by Director Melanie Mandl, with Mark Harvey serving as Keystone Gallery Co-Director. Keystone functions less as a commercial gallery than as a hybrid studio building and public exhibition venue supporting a broad, multidisciplinary Los Angeles art community.

locations.address: 2558 N. San Fernando Rd., Los Angeles, CA 90065

hours_text: Gallery Hours are Tue-Fri 11am-4pm, Sat-Sun 12-5pm, closed Mondays.

notes: Keystone Art Space is a tenant studio complex rather than a traditional commercial gallery; the studio directory lists resident artists by studio number, which are recorded here as 'exhibited' rather than 'represented' since the site does not describe formal representation. An older address (2558 N. San Fernando Rd.) appears in a 2014 news post referring to 'Keystone Gallery' and is listed as a non-current location; current contact information lists only 338 S. Ave 16.

triage.site_notes: Keystone is a working studio/gallery complex organised around a single Squarespace calendar (each show gets its own /calendar/YYYY/M/D/slug page going back to 2013) rather than a separate current/archive split, so individual calendar entries double as the exhibition archive; a studio-directory page serves as the closest thing to an artist roster and /news holds press/blog posts, most of which are too granular to be worth surfacing individually.
